_: Pairs that scripts/lint-twins.mjs flags as alike and that a person has looked at.
An entry is not permission to duplicate. It is a claim that the two are
genuinely different, plus the condition under which that claim expires — so
the next person can check the claim instead of inheriting it.
If a pair stops resembling its twin, the check fails on the stale entry: an
excuse nobody needs any more would silently waive a real duplicate later.

DatePicker ~ DateRangePicker.separated: one date versus an inclusive span: DatePicker's value is a single Date and one pick closes the calendar; DateRangePicker's value is {start, end}, it needs two picks, orders a backwards pair, and its calendar paints the band between the edges. The trigger deliberately wears the same field styling, which is why the markup matches.
DatePicker ~ DateRangePicker.reopenIf: DatePicker learns to accept a span, or DateRangePicker collapses to one pick - a single field doing both jobs is then the smaller thing.

MenuButton ~ MenuIconButton.separated: words versus no words, and the split is the one the system already makes between Button and IconButton. MenuIconButton's `label` is REQUIRED and becomes both the accessible name and the tooltip, because a lone glyph names nothing; MenuButton's label is the visible text and needs neither. Folding them would make that name optional, which is the single thing the separate component exists to prevent. The markup resembles because both hang a Dropdown on a trigger - that mechanism is shared in lib/useAnchoredLayer, which is where sharing belongs here.
MenuButton ~ MenuIconButton.reopenIf: the registry learns to require a prop conditionally on another prop's absence - a MenuButton whose `label` is optional but whose `menuLabel` becomes mandatory when it is missing would then be expressible, and one component is the smaller thing.

RangeSlider ~ Slider.separated: one thumb versus two on one track: Slider's value is a number, RangeSlider's is an ordered [start, end] tuple and each native input clamps against the other. Folding them would make value's type conditional on a prop, and a discriminated props union is exactly what the registry parser cannot express (the Combobox lesson).
RangeSlider ~ Slider.reopenIf: the registry learns to publish a union-typed value, or a third bounded-pair control appears - then one Slider with a range mode is the smaller thing.
